'''Reflections Gold''' is the cancelled Decipher product that got closest to existing. CardGuide numbers it #37 (#36 before the Death Star II starters were split out). Decipher had Lucasfilm-approved art for about 200 cards and wanted to print a last Reflections set before the Star Wars license ended. They ran out of time to playtest. After the license expired they asked Lucasfilm for permission to post the cards as a free PDF; Lucasfilm said no.<ref name="holland">Warren Holland, [https://web.archive.org/web/20080207033202/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/reflectionsgold.html Reflections Gold announcement] at Decipher.com, 25 January 2002 (archive, 7 February 2008)</ref><ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2] (p.201–202) Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

The remastered edition presents reconstructed card images with corrected text. The [[Reflections Gold (original card list)|original playtest list]] preserves the surviving cards, while the [[Reflections Gold (remastered card list)|remastered list]] and [[Reflections Gold (remaster changes)|changes comparison]] show the current remastered versions.

In the 28 December 2001 ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' special broadcast, [[Warren Holland]] described the planned set, internally called ''Reflections Virtual Gold''. It had about 300 new cards built to be easy to collect, with a couple of foil cards in each pack, one of them carrying signatures of Decipher team members. About 100 were "virtual cards": named, numbered and with full statistics, but with a blank game-text box showing only a film logo.<ref name="rfd-special-2430">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1470s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 24:30. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> Each of the four films would have its own display. Their game text was to be posted on a web page run by a Players Committee and changed every four to six months. Decipher proposed that they be tournament legal. Lucasfilm turned the virtual-card concept down.<ref name="rfd-special-1923">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1163s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 19:23. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref>

Warren Holland's public statement of 25 January 2002:<ref name="holland" />

<blockquote>
As I previously announced, it was Decipher's desire to "give" players 200 ''Star Wars'' CCG cards (in PDF format on our web site) that had already been approved by Lucasfilm for Reflections Gold. We saw this as a gift to players for all their support throughout the years. We were not able to print these cards as we had hoped, but we didn't want to see all the art and gameplay go to waste.

I am sorry to announce that Lucasfilm has just rejected the idea of us releasing these cards for free on the web. Unfortunately, we will never be able to show these cards to the general public. We don't agree with this decision by Lucasfilm, but we have to abide by it. Sorry.

Warren Holland, Chairman & CEO, Decipher Inc.
</blockquote>

Playtest copies still left Decipher: images printed on sticker stock and stuck to white-border cards. A near-complete set reached the secondary market in 2006 and was partly destroyed in a household accident. The remaining extras and scans went to Category One Games and the Players Committee.<ref name="c1">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/reflectionsgold/ Reflections Gold] at Category One Games. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927194326/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/reflectionsgold/ Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="forum">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?f=87&t=18282 Reflections Gold, Playtest, Signed, Cards etc] at forum.starwarsccg.org (t=18282). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021002530/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t18282-f87.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Design features ==
Reflections Gold introduced credits as a new game concept alongside combo cards and cards with blank game-text boxes.<ref name="forum" /><ref name="c1" /><ref name="cg">[https://web.archive.org/web/20250222210013/https://cardguide.fandom.com/wiki/Reflections_Gold_(expansion) Reflections Gold (expansion)] at CardGuide Wiki (archive, 22 February 2025)</ref>

=== Credits ===
Under the proposed credit concept, a player would start with 4 or 5 credit points and could keep matching "wide vision" cards in the opening hand. Each of those cards showed gold credit coins in the lower right. They were existing cards with the image turned sideways.<ref name="c1" />

=== Combo cards and blank cards ===
* '''Combo cards''' — interrupt and effect pairs in the Reflections II / Coruscant style. Players considered them overpowered because each half was already strong alone; the usual forum example is Beggar & Revolution.
* '''Blank cards''' — new frames with an empty text box. Decipher's idea was that the coming Players Committee could rotate printed text into those boxes every few months. That plan is the ancestor of virtual cards; after Lucasfilm refused the PDF giveaway, the PC built virtual cards without Decipher's pre-printed blanks.<ref name="c1" />

== How the copies survived ==
A former seller close to Decipher staff sold extras in late 2006, then reported that an accident had destroyed most of a full set. Leftover extras went to Category One,<ref name="c1" /> and the seller later gave the Players Committee a scan of each card. The sticker playtests are poorly printed; because they were barely tested, surviving copies are often in good physical shape.<ref name="c1" />

The scans were first posted in a Players Committee forum thread as Category One Photobucket albums, mixed with Dagobah playtests and signed cards.<ref name="forum" /><ref name="encyc" />

A later Google document, ''Reflections Gold Remastered'', rebuilds the frames as cleaned card images (blank text boxes, corrected layout) from those playtest stickers. It is not a Decipher print file.<ref name="doc">[https://docs.google.com/document/d/17TqWsm6AtmGREZlerTsMWjy5K9qfaamf/edit Reflections Gold Remastered] (Google Doc). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927194356/https://docs.google.com/document/d/17TqWsm6AtmGREZlerTsMWjy5K9qfaamf/edit Internet Archive]</ref>

Category One still lists singles. A 2026 r/starwarsccg thread tracks which physical copies collectors believe still exist.<ref name="reddit">[https://www.reddit.com/r/starwarsccg/comments/1t4kb7c/reflections_gold_history_tracker/ Reflections Gold history tracker] on Reddit Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195008/https://www.reddit.com/r/starwarsccg/comments/1t4kb7c/reflections_gold_history_tracker/ Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="buylist">[https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398 Category One Games Reflections Gold buylist] (310 titles; pages 1–13). Preserved copies (27 September 2026): [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927193408/https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398?page=2&sort_by_price=0 p2], [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927193458/https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398?page=4&sort_by_price=0 p4], [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927193535/https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398?page=5&sort_by_price=0 p5], [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927193653/https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398?page=6&sort_by_price=0 p6], [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927193802/https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398?page=8&sort_by_price=0 p8], [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927193838/https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398?page=9&sort_by_price=0 p9], [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927194027/https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398?page=11&sort_by_price=0 p11], [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927194101/https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398?page=12&sort_by_price=0 p12], [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927194212/https://www.categoryonegames.com/buylist/star_wars_ccg-reflections_gold/398?page=13&sort_by_price=0 p13]</ref>
